reranked_evidence.title: Indian Prime Minister Appeals for Calm After Deadly Riots Wrack New Delhi
reranked_evidence.snippet: Policemen move in a truck in a riot affected area after clashes erupted between people demonstrating for and against a new citizenship law in New Delhi, India, Feb. 26, 2020. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is appealing for calm after three days of deadly clashes between Hindus and Muslim groups in the Indian capital left at least 23 people dead and more than 200 injured. The rioting that wracked a neighborhood on the fringes of the city were the worst witnessed in New Delhi in recent decades and coincided with a visit by U.S. President Donald Trump to India. In a tweet Prime Minister Modi said "Peace and harmony are central to our ethos. The clashes erupted after Muslim Protesters occupied a road in New Delhi neighborhood on Saturday to protest the new citizenship law that makes fast-tracked Indian citizenship available to immigrants from three neighboring countries, except Muslims.
